articles.title: Chuva prejudica produção de cebolinha em Mogi, diz agricultor | G1
articles.standfirst: Segundo Josué Barbosa, o problema não é apenas o alagamento da plantação, mas também a perda do adubo. Mogi está entre as cidades com os maiores acumulados de chuva nas últimas 24 horas no estado de São Paulo.
articles.summary: Segundo Josué Barbosa, o problema não é apenas o alagamento da plantação, mas também a perda do adubo. Mogi está entre as cidades com os maiores acumulados de chuva.
articles.body:
A chuva das últimas 24 horas causou prejuízos na agricultura de Mogi das Cruzes . O produtor rural Josué Barbosa estima ter perdido 30% da produção de cebolinha por causa do excesso de água no solo. A propriedade fica na Chácara dos Baianos, no distrito de Jundiapeba.

Segundo dados do Centro Nacional de Monitoramento e Alertas de Desastres Naturais (Cemaden) e do Instituto Nacional de Meteorologia (Inmet), foram registrados 55 milímetros de chuva em Jundiapeba nas últimas 24 horas.

Agricultor Josué Barbosa afirma que perdeu 30% da produção de cebolinha por causa da chuva — Foto: Maiara Barbosa/TV Diário

Barbosa explica que a chuva em excesso leva os nutrientes do solo. Segundo ele, o problema não é apenas o alagamento da plantação, mas também a perda do adubo. Com isso, as cebolinhas ficam amareladas e secas.

“Desmanchando com excesso de água e não presta para ir para o comércio. Na roça está nessas condições e se colher e mandar para o comércio, ela chega podre e por isso que vem a perda”, afirma o agricultor.

Outro problema, segundo Barbosa, é o solo encharcado, que impede o plantio em alguns terrenos.

Canteiro ficou com o solo encharcado em propriedade rural de Mogi das Cruzes — Foto: Maiara Barbosa/ TV Diário

articles.title: Empresa abre vaga de trainee no Maranhão com salário de R$ 7,5 mil | G1
articles.standfirst: Oportunidade é voltada para a área de Logística. Inscrições seguem até 28 de setembro e programa terá duração de 18 meses.
articles.summary: Oportunidade é voltada para a área de Logística. Inscrições seguem até 28 de setembro e programa terá duração de 18 meses.
articles.body:
Oportunidade é voltada para a área de Logística. Inscrições seguem até 28 de setembro e programa terá duração de 18 meses. — Foto: Divulgação/Solar Coca-Cola

A Solar Coca-Cola abriu inscrições para um programa de trainee com vaga no Maranhão. A oportunidade no estado é voltada para a área de Logística e oferece salário de R$ 7,5 mil, além de benefícios.

As inscrições podem ser feitas até o dia 28 de setembro pela página oficial do programa. A seleção também oferece vagas em outros estados, nas áreas de Engenharia, Logística e Manutenção.

Para participar, é necessário ter formação de nível superior, em cursos de bacharelado, licenciatura ou tecnólogo, nas áreas de Logística, Manutenção ou Engenharia. A conclusão do curso deve ocorrer entre janeiro de 2021 e dezembro de 2026.

Os candidatos também precisam ter disponibilidade para trabalhar presencialmente durante os 18 meses de duração do programa. Além do Maranhão, há oportunidades para Engenharia no Ceará, Logística em Alagoas e Manutenção na Bahia e em Mato Grosso.

Além do salário de R$ 7,5 mil, os selecionados terão direito a benefícios como vale-refeição ou alimentação em refeitório, vale-transporte ou transporte fretado, plano de saúde, plano odontológico, seguro de vida e participação nos resultados.

A empresa também oferece benefícios como Wellhub, descontos em produtos, programa de saúde emocional e telemedicina.

O processo seletivo será dividido em sete etapas. Após as inscrições, previstas para setembro, os candidatos passarão por entrevistas remotas e vídeo-entrevista em outubro.

Em novembro, estão previstas dinâmicas e novas entrevistas online. A etapa presencial será realizada em dezembro.

A admissão dos aprovados está prevista para janeiro.

Segundo a Solar Coca-Cola, o programa tem foco na formação de profissionais para atuar na área de Supply Chain, que envolve processos como logística, manutenção e operações industriais.

articles.title: Quatro jovens são presos no Canadá por arrombarem lojas usando carros para roubar joias e cartas colecionáveis; VÍDEO | G1
articles.standfirst: Os suspeitos utilizavam veículos roubados para bater contra portas e vitrines dos estabelecimentos e abrir caminho para os furtos. Polícia apura que o prejuízo chegou a quase R$ 800 mil.
articles.summary: Os suspeitos utilizavam veículos roubados para bater contra portas e vitrines dos estabelecimentos e abrir caminho para os furtos. Polícia apura que o prejuízo chegou a quase R$ 800 mil.
articles.body:
Quatro jovens, com idades entre 15 e 18 anos, foram presos no Canadá e são acusados de participar de uma onda de invasões e roubos a estabelecimentos comerciais na região da Grande Toronto e em Durham. Segundo a polícia, o grupo está ligado a 36 incidentes criminosos e enfrenta mais de 200 acusações.

A investigação, chamada de "Project Magenta", começou em junho de 2026, depois que duas lojas de cartas colecionáveis foram arrombadas em Ajax, na província de Ontário.

Em um dos casos, ocorrido em 14 de junho, os suspeitos levaram cerca de US$ 148 mil em mercadorias (ou cerca de R$ 752 mil) .

Segundo a Polícia Regional de Durham, os jovens também tinham como alvos joalherias, lojas de produtos de cannabis e casas de penhores .

Jovens usavam carros roubados para quebrar vidraças e roubar itens. — Foto: Reprodução/Facebook/Durham Regional Police Service

O grupo é acusado de usar um método conhecido como smash-and-grab . Os suspeitos utilizavam veículos roubados para bater contra portas e vitrines dos estabelecimentos e abrir caminho para os furtos.

Após as invasões, os carros eram abandonados e substituídos por outros veículos também roubados para novas ações, segundo os investigadores.

Entre junho e setembro, a polícia associou os quatro a 36 incidentes em Toronto e na Região de Durham. Os casos incluem oito invasões comerciais, 15 crimes relacionados a furtos de veículos, roubo de placas, furtos dentro de carros estacionados, tentativas de roubo de veículos e fraudes.

As perdas financeiras e os danos provocados pelos crimes são estimados em quase US$ 1 milhão , segundo a polícia. O valor pode aumentar com a identificação de novas vítimas.

Entre os quatro presos, dois são maiores de idade.

Mahith Sivananthan, de 18 anos, morador de Pickering, responde por acusações que incluem posse de bens obtidos por crime, invasão de propriedade, uso de disfarce com intenção criminosa, furto de veículos e danos ao patrimônio .

Mohammad Sakrak, também de 18 anos e morador de Toronto, é acusado de posse de propriedade roubada, furto de veículo e uso de disfarce com intenção criminosa.

Os outros dois acusados têm 16 e 15 anos. As identidades deles não foram divulgadas. O mais novo, de 15 anos, enfrenta acusações que incluem roubo, invasão de propriedade, furto de veículos e posse de instrumentos para arrombamento . Os quatro permanecem sob custódia e aguardam audiência de fiança.

Grupo usava carros para quebrar vidraças. — Foto: Reprodução/Facebook/Durham Regional Police Service

Durante o cumprimento de mandados de busca em residências na região da Grande Toronto, os policiais recuperaram diversos bens relacionados aos crimes.

O detetive-sargento Dave Davies afirmou que as prisões representam uma interrupção significativa da rede criminosa. Segundo ele, novas acusações podem ser apresentadas à medida que as provas forem analisadas.

O chefe da Polícia Regional de Durham, Peter Moreira, também alertou para a exploração de jovens por redes criminosas organizadas. Ele defendeu uma revisão da legislação penal juvenil e do Código Criminal do Canadá.

A investigação continua. A polícia pede que pessoas que tenham informações ou imagens de câmeras de segurança relacionadas aos crimes procurem os investigadores.

articles.title: Fim de semana tem previsão de rachadas e tornados em regiões do país  | G1
articles.standfirst: Frente fria e ciclone extratropical favorecem temporais em estados do Sul e Sudeste; acumulados podem chegar a 100 milímetros
articles.summary: Frente fria e ciclone extratropical favorecem temporais em estados do Sul e Sudeste; acumulados podem chegar a 100 milímetros
articles.body:
O fim de semana deve ser marcado por chuva forte e ventos intensos em diversas áreas do Sul, Sudeste e Centro-Oeste do país. Segundo a previsão apresentada pelo Instituto Nacional de Meteorologia (Inmet), os acumulados de chuva podem chegar a 100 milímetros em algumas regiões.

O alerta abrange praticamente todo o Rio Grande do Sul, Santa Catarina e Paraná, além de grande parte de Mato Grosso do Sul, áreas de São Paulo, Minas Gerais e Rio de Janeiro. Também há previsão de chuva em pontos de Mato Grosso e Rondônia.

A situação é influenciada pela formação de um ciclone extratropical e de uma frente fria. O sistema também deve provocar uma mudança nas temperaturas ao longo do fim de semana.

Além da chuva, há previsão de ventos fortes. Nesta sexta-feira (11) e no sábado (12), as rajadas podem chegar a 90 km/h em áreas do norte do Rio Grande do Sul, Santa Catarina, Paraná, Mato Grosso do Sul e no sul de São Paulo.

No sábado, os ventos ainda podem atingir 70 km/h em áreas do litoral de Santa Catarina, Paraná e São Paulo e Rio de Janeiro.

O Paraná está entre os estados que exigem maior atenção. Segundo a previsão, o risco de temporais permanece nesta sexta-feira (11), inclusive com possibilidade de tornados.

A região já foi atingida por eventos severos nos últimos dias. Cerca de 30 cidades foram afetadas no estado e duas tiveram registros de tornados.

Em Dois Vizinhos, no oeste do Paraná, mais de 600 casas ficaram sem telhado após a passagem de granizo. Cerca de 10 mil imóveis ainda estavam sem energia elétrica.

A passagem da frente fria também deve provocar queda nas temperaturas em algumas áreas. A previsão é de que Campo Grande, por exemplo, registre temperaturas mais baixas no sábado.

Em algumas áreas, no entanto, as temperaturas haviam subido antes da chegada do sistema.

A previsão também é acompanhada pela expectativa de um El Niño muito forte nos próximos meses. Segundo a informação apresentada no telejornal, há 98% de chance de o fenômeno permanecer muito forte em novembro e dezembro.

Especialistas afirmam que a intensidade esperada seria excepcional em comparação com os registros disponíveis desde o início das medições da NOAA, em 1950.

Sul do Brasil fica em alerta vermelho para temporais; chuva avança pelo país no fim de semana — Foto: Reprodução/TV Globo

articles.title: Ribeirão Quilombo transborda e alaga casas em Nova Odessa | G1
articles.standfirst: Elevação do Ribeirão Quilombo na madrugada desta sexta-feira (11) causou transtornos e Defesa Civil precisou resgatar motorista ilhada. Casas foram invadidas pela água.
articles.summary: O Ribeirão Quilombo transbordou em Nova Odessa nesta sexta-feira (11), atingindo residências e exigindo resgates da Defesa Civil em diversos bairros alagados.
articles.body:
Ribeirão Quilombo transborda em Nova Odessa (SP) — Foto: Márcio Silveira/EPTV

O Ribeirão Quilombo, em Nova Odessa (SP), começou a subir durante a madrugada desta sexta-feira (11) e inundou ruas do bairro Vila Azenha. Segundo a prefeitura, a água também invadiu duas casas no Jardim Flórida e uma no Jardim Lopes Iglesias.

Uma motorista precisou ser resgatada, mas sem gravidade, e as famílias atingidas estão recebendo alimentação e sendo levadas para a casa de parentes, informou a administração municipal.

Moradores relatam à EPTV , afiliada da TV Globo, que o problema é recorrente na região e cobraram a conclusão de uma obra de escoamento.

"A minha casa fica já ilhada, a gente não pode sair. [...] A gente já está indo para quase para um ano e meio, ninguém resolve nada, eles falam que não tem nem funcionário no setor de obra e nem dinheiro para a obra", afirma o morador Sérgio Polastrini sobre o trabalho de prevenção da prefeitura.

A aposentada Benedita de Lima também teve a residência tomada pela água do ribeirão e perdeu mantimentos.

"Está cheio de água, o matimento meu já molhou tudo. E não é de hoje que a gente está falando para eles virem arrumar. [...] Toda vez que chover é isso daí", lamenta a moradora.

" O ano passado veio no outubro e novembro na minha casa também, e eu só estou ali porque eu não tenho condições de pagar aluguel", complementa.

A prefeitura de Nova Odessa informou que as equipes da Defesa Civil monitoram a situação e orientam os moradores a evitarem áreas alagadas. No entanto, não respondeu às reclamações de falta de obras e manutenção apontadas pelos moradores até a última atualização desta reportagem.

Ribeirão Quilombo transborda e invade ruas em Nova Odessa (SP) — Foto: Marcio Silveira/EPTV

articles.title: Tecnologias novas da Bayer abrangem múltiplas fases da mosca-da-fruta | G1
articles.standfirst: Produtos combinam ação de choque imediata e garante controle residual mais prolongado.
articles.summary: Produtos combinam ação de choque imediata e garante controle residual mais prolongado.
articles.body:
3_Dupla da Bayer atua em todas as fases da mosca-da-fruta, de formas diferentes_Seiva do Vale — Foto: Acervo/Seiva do Vale

Na guerra contra a temida mosca-da-fruta, os fruticultores do Vale do São Francisco contam com duas novas tecnologias desenvolvidas pela Bayer. Elas contribuem no manejo integrado e eficaz contra a praga, que tem grande potencial de gerar prejuízo ao produtor. As soluções Sivanto Prime e Decis 25 EC prometem maior controle e segurança para diversas culturas regionais, especialmente a manga. Elas atuam de formas diferentes para ampliar as estratégias usadas pelo produtor.

A alternância e o manejo combinado dessas duas ferramentas oferecem aos produtores mais opções e flexibilidade. O Decis 25 EC entra com uma ação de choque imediata, enquanto o Sivanto Prime garante um controle residual mais prolongado, abrangendo múltiplas fases da praga. Essa estratégia permite que o produtor ajuste o manejo de acordo com a situação de sua área e o estágio da praga, garantindo maior eficácia no controle da mosca-da-fruta.

O Sivanto Prime é um produto com características únicas no mercado: ele age tanto pelo contato, quanto sistêmico e translaminar, o que garante um período maior de controle.

Na ação sistêmica, o produto é absorvido e entra nos vasos condutores de seiva da planta. E na ação por contato, ele fica na superfície da planta e forma uma barreira protetora.

Já na ação translaminar é referente à capacidade de um produto atravessar a lâmina da folha, protegendo tanto o topo quanto a parte de baixo. Isso permite que atingir pragas escondidas na parte inferior, mesmo que o produto tenha sido pulverizado apenas por cima.

Além disso, ele atua em diversas fases do ciclo da praga, incluindo ovos, ninfas (larvas após o ovo) e adultos. Também apresenta alta segurança e eficiência especificamente contra pragas com comportamento igual a mosca-da-fruta e oferece um longo período residual de controle.

O Decis 25 EC, por sua vez, é um produto de contato com ação de choque, pertencente ao grupo dos piretroides, que são inseticidas sintéticos desenvolvidos em laboratório a partir de fórmulas vegetais para durarem mais tempo sob a luz do sol.

Ele atua fortemente nos adultos da mosca-da-fruta e pode ser aplicado até 20 dias antes da colheita, assim como o Sivanto Prime, proporcionando segurança para os produtores tanto no mercado interno quanto para exportação.

articles.title: Erdogan: The Making of Modern Turkiye
articles.summary: An interview with Turkish President Erdogan on foreign policy, regional conflicts and 25 years of AK Party rule.
articles.body:
At a time of global upheaval, one man has redrawn Turkiye’s political map. In an exclusive interview with Al Jazeera, Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan reflects on more than two decades in power.

His rise began in the early 1990s, when he was elected mayor of Istanbul. He founded the Justice and Development Party, or AK Party, in 2001 and has won every election since then. After three terms as prime minister, he was elected president in 2014 and remains in office to date.

Marking the 25th anniversary of the AK Party, Erdogan talks to Al Jazeera Arabic’s Ali Al Dafiri about Turkiye’s growing role in the shifting geopolitical landscape, highlighting the recent defence deal he concluded with Saudi Arabia and Pakistan. He addresses the US-Israel war on Iran, advocating for open maritime navigation in the Strait of Hormuz while identifying Israel as the primary driver of the regional conflict. He also affirms Turkiye’s solid support for Syria’s new administration and his unwavering solidarity with Lebanon and Gaza. On a domestic level, Erdogan reflects on Turkiye’s sweeping economic transformation and its future, stating that European Union accession is no longer a priority.

articles.title: VÍDEO: estátua de Charlie Kirk aparece em NY um ano após sua morte | G1
articles.standfirst: Artista italiano afirmou que gastou US$ 100 mil para fazer homenagem. Ativista conservador foi assassinado a tiros durante evento em universidade em Utah em 10 de setembro de 2025.
articles.summary: Artista italiano afirmou que gastou US$ 100 mil para fazer homenagem. Ativista conservador foi assassinado a tiros durante evento em universidade em Utah em 10 de setembro de 2025.
articles.body:
Uma estátua do ativista conservador Charlie Kirk foi revelada na Times Square , em Nova York , na quinta-feira (10), no dia que marcou um ano de seu assassinato.

A estátua em tamanho real, feita com uma estrutura metálica coberta de resina, retrata Kirk segurando um microfone e vestindo um moletom com a palavra "Liberdade" em letras garrafais. O artista Sergio Furnari, dono da obra, afirmou que gastou US$ 100 mil (R$ 510 mil) do próprio bolso com materiais e mão de obra. Veja no vídeo acima.

Kirk foi morto aos 31 anos em 10 de setembro de 2025 com um tiro no pescoço durante um debate com estudantes na universidade de Utah Valley.

Estátua de Charlie Kirk feita por artista italiano Sergio Furnari revelada na Times Square, em Nova York, nos Estados Unidos, em 10 de setembro de 2026. — Foto: REUTERS/Brendan McDermid

Furnari pediu calma antes da inauguração, enquanto o ativista de extrema direita Jake Lang gritava palavras de ordem contra o prefeito de Nova York, Zohran Mamdani.

Lang, que recebeu um perdão do presidente dos EUA, Donald Trump, por seu envolvimento no ataque ao Capitólio dos EUA em 6 de janeiro de 2021, participou da inauguração ao lado de Furnari.

“Lutem por Charlie! Lutem por Charlie!”, gritou Lang durante a inauguração. O ativista de extrema direita disse também que Kirk será lembrado como um herói nacional.

No ano desde o assassinato de Kirk, a Turning Point USA, organização que ele cofundou, ampliou sua presença em faculdades e escolas de ensino médio. O grupo afirmou que atualmente possui mais de 3.500 núcleos em escolas de ensino médio em todo o país, um aumento de 180%, e mais de 1.500 núcleos em universidades, uma alta de mais de 60% desde a morte de Kirk.

Ativista de extrema direita Jake Lang ao lado de estátua de Charlie Kirk na Times Square, em Nova York, nos Estados Unidos, em 10 de setembro de 2026. — Foto: REUTERS/Brendan McDermid

articles.title: VÍDEO: Chuva alaga ruas e invade casa em Vassouras | G1
articles.standfirst: Pancada d'água atingiu pico de 42,9 mm/h na noite de quinta-feira; agentes municipais atuam nos locais atingidos e não há desabrigados.
articles.summary: Pancada d'água atingiu pico de 42,9 mm/h na noite de quinta-feira; agentes municipais atuam nos locais atingidos e não há desabrigados.
articles.body:
A chuva forte que atingiu Vassouras (RJ) na noite de quinta-feira (10) provocou alagamentos e transtornos em ruas do município. Segundo a Defesa Civil, o índice pluviométrico alcançou um pico de intensidade de 42,9 mm/h.

De acordo com o órgão, foram registrados dois pontos principais de alagamento: na Rua Paulo Torres, no Centro, e na Rua Otávio Gomes, no bairro Madruga.

A Defesa Civil informou ainda que a água invadiu uma residência pela ausência de um muro de contenção no terreno.

Equipes da Prefeitura de Vassouras atuam nos locais afetados para prestar assistência aos moradores e realizar reparos. Não houve registro de feridos, desabrigados ou desalojados.

articles.title: VÍDEO: carros são arrastados por enxurrada de lama em Chapecó | G1
articles.standfirst: Câmeras de segurança registraram o grande volume invadindo o estacionamento. Força da água arrastou os veículos.
articles.summary: Câmeras de segurança registraram a enxurrada de água e lama invadindo o local. Força da água arrastou os carros estacionados.
articles.body:
Dois muros desabaram na manhã desta sexta-feira (11) em Chapecó , no Oeste de Santa Catarina , e atingiram a garagem de um prédio residencial. O caso ocorreu por volta das 8h, no bairro Pinheirinho, durante uma forte chuva ( assista acima ).

Câmeras de segurança registraram o momento em que as estruturas cederam, invadindo a garagem com água e lama. A força da enxurrada arrastou os carros que estavam estacionados . Ninguém ficou ferido.

Queda de muro arrasta carros e provoca enxurrada de lama em garagem de prédio em Chapecó — Foto: Reprodução/NSC TV

Ao g1 , o síndico do condomínio, Ivan Breitenbach, relatou que estava perto da garagem quando ouviu o barulho do desabamento.

"A gente escutou um estrondo grande, até achou que era um raio, mas aí saiu para fora e verificou e era o muro que tinha rompido, tinha estourado e caído" disse.

Breitenbach explicou que os muros pertencem a duas construções vizinhas que estão em obras, localizadas em um nível acima do prédio residencial. A Defesa Civil foi acionada e isolou o local.

Cerca de 15 veículos estavam na garagem no momento do desabamento. Apenas um carro ficou preso sob a cobertura metálica, que cedeu com o impacto.

Garagem foi atingida após chuva em Chapecó, no Oeste de Santa Catarina — Foto: Suzi gobbi/Arquivo Pessoal

Temporais e granizo atingiram outras cidades do Oeste e Meio-Oeste de Santa Catarina entre a noite de quinta-feira (10) e a manhã desta sexta-feira (11). A chuva causou causou alagamentos e estragos em casas em outras cidades da região além de Chapecó.

articles.title: Por que a presença de Mamdani, muçulmano, é contestada por republicanos e parentes das vítimas do 11/9 | G1
articles.standfirst: Cerimônia para homenagear os mortos do atentado em NY ganha contornos islamofóbicos e rejeição ao atual prefeito.
articles.summary: Cerimônia para homenagear os mortos do atentado em NY ganha contornos islamofóbicos e rejeição ao atual prefeito.
articles.body:
O prefeito de Nova York, Zohran Mamdani, chega para cerimônia em memória às vítimas dos ataques de 11 de setembro de 2001, em Nova York, em 11 de setembro de 2026. — Foto: Adam Gray/ Pool via Reuters

Vinte e cinco anos após enfrentar sua maior tragédia, Nova York tem um prefeito muçulmano , o socialista democrático Zohran Mamdani. Mas seus detratores fizeram de tudo para mantê-lo longe da cerimônia que homenageia os cerca de três mil mortos nos atentados às Torres Gêmeas.

Como um reflexo da realidade cada vez mais divisiva do país, o espírito de união que tradicionalmente marcou o tributo deu lugar, este ano, à discórdia partidária, personificada na figura do jovem prefeito.

➡️ Uma petição com mais de 110 mil assinaturas, incluindo parentes das vítimas, pediu que Mamdani não comparecesse às homenagens no Marco Zero , alegando que ele é “insuficientemente crítico das ideologias extremistas”.

O ex-prefeito Rudy Giuliani e o ex-governador George Pataki, que estavam nos cargos no dia 11 de setembro de 2001, corroboram a tese de que o prefeito é persona non grata no tributo .

Giuliani, que emergiu como símbolo da liderança da cidade após os atentados, hoje amarga o ostracismo político e chegou a divulgar teorias da conspiração de teor islamofóbico sobre o atual prefeito, dizendo-se ofendido com sua presença na cerimônia. Sugeriu, por exemplo, que, para Mamdani, os ataques de 11 de Setembro não foram atos terroristas.

O republicano Bruce Blakeman, que aspira o governo de Nova York, pediu aos participantes da cerimônia que dessem as costas a Mamdani durante a leitura dos nomes das vítimas: “Ele não é bem-vindo porque ainda não disse nada em oposição à expressão ‘globalizar a Intifada’".

Outros argumentos rondavam a insistência para que o prefeito fique de fora das homenagens: as ligações com o comentarista Hasan Piker, que afirmou, mas depois se desculpou, que "os EUA mereceram o 11 de Setembro”. A declaração foi condenada pelo prefeito .

Com um simples gesto, Mamdani recentemente desatou a fúria das famílias das vítimas, ao entregar a caneta com que assinou ordens executivas sobre as comemorações do 25 aniversário do atentado a seu principal conselheiro, Ramzi Kassem.

Como advogado, Kassem defendeu um integrante da al-Qaeda que era cunhado de um dos sequestradores do 11 de Setembro.

“Sentimos que a presença de Mamdani seria uma falta de respeito com os membros da nossa família, devido às pessoas que ele apoia”, afirmou um dos autores da petição, Giovanni Galante, que perdeu a esposa Grace no atentado.

A animosidade tem contornos políticos e islamofóbicos . O prefeito resistiu com firmeza à rejeição dos que tentam associá-lo, como muçulmano, a um representante dos 19 terroristas do 11 de Setembro e confirmou a presença no evento.

"Tenho orgulho de ser o prefeito desta cidade, amo esta cidade, amo este país e o que eu quero que seja o foco desta semana são as famílias cujos entes queridos foram tirados delas há 25 anos no horrível ato de terror de 11 de Setembro".

Apesar dos protestos, Zohran foi à cerimônia, nesta manhã.

articles.title: Atos em Nova York e no Pentágono marcam os 25 anos do 11 de Setembro | G1
articles.standfirst: Vice-presidente J.D. Vance participou de homenagem em Nova York no Memorial onde ficavam as Torres Gêmeas. Presidente dos EUA, Donald Trump, fará discurso na sede do Departamento de Guerra. Atentado da Al-Qaeda matou quase três mil pessoas.
articles.summary: Vice-presidente J.D. Vance participou de homenagem em Nova York no Memorial onde ficavam as Torres Gêmeas. Presidente dos EUA, Donald Trump, fará discurso na sede do Departamento de Guerra. Atentado da Al-Qaeda matou quase três mil pessoas.
articles.body:
Ato de homenagem aos 25 anos do atentado de 11 de Setembro em Nova York, nos Estados Unidos, em 11 de setembro de 2026. — Foto: REUTERS/Jeenah Moon/Pool

Atos em Nova York , no Pentágono e em outras cidades pelos Estados Unidos marcaram nesta sexta-feira (11) os 25 anos do atentado de 11 de Setembro, que destruiu as Torres Gêmeas e deixaram quase três mil mortos.

Uma homenagem em Nova York no Memorial do 11 de Setembro, onde as Torres Gêmeas ficavam, foi marcada por momentos de silêncio e familiares das vítimas lendo em voz alta os nomes dos 2.977 mortos no atentado. O vice-presidente dos EUA, J.D. Vance, e todos os ex-presidentes vivos, como Joe Biden, George Bush, Barack Obama e Bill Clinton compareceram ao ato.

O prefeito de Nova York, Zohran Mamdani, também esteve presente na homenagem, apesar de ter enfrentado resistência da população para participar por conta dele ser muçulmano e porque um de seus conselheiros foi advogado de um membro da Al-Qaeda —grupo terrorista que protagonizou o atentado.

O presidente dos EUA, Donald Trump , e o secretário de Guerra, Pete Hegseth, participaram de uma homenagem no Pentágono, em Washington D.C.

Em discurso, Trump afirmou que os "EUA se viram de frente ao mal genuíno" no dia 11 de Setembro de 2001. Ele também lembrou a memória das vítimas dos voos sequestrados pela Al-Qaeda.

"2.977 almas lindas foram extirpadas do nosso mundo e milhares outras nos anos seguintes por causa daquele atentado grotesco. Nunca nunca vamos esquecer, e é por isso que lutamos hoje. Não temos escolha, só pode haver vitória. Lutamos forte e para vencer. (...) Foi um mal horrível e imenso, que pretendia destruir tudo que é de bom. Mas hoje lembramos também como nosso país respondeu a essa perversão. Lembramos naquela época e até hoje do que somos feitos", afirmou Trump.

Hegseth também discursou, e em sua fala ele elogiou as equipes de emergência e a população, "heróis que encararam a morte de frente".

"O 11 de Setembro foi um dos dias mais sombrios na história dos EUA, mas o mal não conseguiu prevalecer. 25 anos depois, os EUA continuam fortes e orgulhosos como nunca. (...) Até hoje ainda estamos mandando terroristas para o inferno, que é onde eles pertencem. Vamos terminar esta luta", afirmou.

Outros atos em outras cidades dos EUA e pelo mundo também homenagearam a memória das vítimas do atentado. Atos foram registrados em Arlington, na Virgínia, em Shanksville, na Pensilvânia, e na sede da Otan, na Bélgica.

Veja abaixo fotos das homenagens pelos 25 anos do 11 de Setembro:

Homenagem às vítimas do atentado de 11 de Setembro em Nova York, nos Estados Unidos, em 11 de setembro de 2026. — Foto: REUTERS/Jeenah Moon/Pool

Policial presta homenagem a vítimas do 11 de Setembro durante homenagem de 25 anos do atentado em Nova York, nos Estados Unidos, em 11 de setembro de 2026. — Foto: REUTERS/Jeenah Moon/Pool

Presidente dos Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, durante homenagem às vítimas do atentado de 11 de Setembro no Pentágono, nos EUA, em 11 de setembro de 2026. — Foto: REUTERS/Elizabeth Frantz

Homenagem às vítimas do atentado de 11 de Setembro em Nova York, nos Estados Unidos, em 11 de setembro de 2026. — Foto: Hiroko Masuike/Pool via REUTERS

Homenagem às vítimas do atentado de 11 de Setembro em Nova York, nos Estados Unidos, em 11 de setembro de 2026. — Foto: Spencer Platt/Pool via REUTERS

Dois aviões que foram sequestrados por terroristas da Al-Qaeda se chocaram contra as Torres Gêmeas em 11 de Setembro de 2001. Os prédios, à época os mais altos de Nova York, caíram e 2.977 pessoas morreram.

Às 8h46, no horário local, o primeiro avião atingiu a Torre Norte do World Trade Center. Dezessete minutos depois, às 9h03, um segundo avião colidiu contra a Torre Sul.

O ataque às Torres Gêmeas foi coordenado com outros que atingiram outros alvos pelos Estados Unidos.

Um terceiro avião foi lançado contra o Pentágono , sede do Departamento de Defesa dos EUA, em Washington D.C.

Um quarto avião caiu em uma área rural próxima a Shanksville, na Pensilvânia. A aeronave não chegou ao destino pretendido pelos sequestradores porque passageiros reagiram ao sequestro e enfrentaram os criminosos.

Milhares de outras pessoas morreram ao longo dos anos em Nova York por conta de problemas respiratórios causados pela fumaça tóxica liberada pela queda dos edifícios. Mais pessoas morreram após o atentado que no dia do atentado, inclusive, segundo o governo dos EUA.

articles.title: The Indian Cowboy rides again: Australia-India feature film inspired by Bobby Cash announced
articles.summary: Rest of World News: NEW DELHI: A new Australia-India feature film inspired by the life of country singer Bobby Cash, who rose to prominence in Australia's country music s.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: A new Australia-India feature film inspired by the life of country singer Bobby Cash, who rose to prominence in Australia's country music scene after moving from Dehradun to Tamworth, was announced by New South Wales Premier Chris Minns at a reception hosted by Australian High Commissioner to India Philip Green OAM.The film will be directed by Sydney-based filmmaker Anupam Sharma, with award-winning NSW writer-director Victoria Wharfe McIntyre as screenwriter and Satish Sharma as Indian co-producer.The project draws inspiration from Cash's journey from the mountains of Dehradun to Tamworth, the capital of Australian country music, where he became known as "The Indian Cowboy".NSW Premier Chris Minns said Cash's story reflected the connection between India and New South Wales."Bobby's story is a great example of the connection between India and NSW - a musician from Dehradun who found an audience and a home in Australian country music. It's fantastic to see that story now being made into a film in NSW, bringing Indian and Australian talent together on screen," Minns said.Sharma said the story represented the cultural connection between the two countries and described the film as a story of music, migration and identity."Bobby's is a story India gave Australia, and Australia gave back. Twenty years on, it still tells you everything about what these two countries can be to each other," Sharma said.He added, "From the regional Himalayas to regional New South Wales - the Indian Cowboy rides again."Cash said his journey began when he left Dehradun with a guitar and found a stage in Australia."Australia gave me a stage, and Tamworth gave me a name. Country music is about where you come from - mine just happens to be the Himalayas," Cash said.He added that he hoped the film would convey the idea that music can transcend borders.The film is being positioned as more than a biopic, exploring themes of music, migration and identity through Cash's journey between India and Australia.Screenwriter Victoria Wharfe McIntyre said Cash's story offered an opportunity to explore cultural contrasts and the connections created through music."Bobby Cash walks that line and through his music brings together worlds that could not be more different. Regional Himalayas to Regional NSW," she said.Calling it "an incredible true Australian-Indian story", McIntyre said she was grateful to tell the story alongside Sharma.Indian co-producer Satish Sharma highlighted the project's connection to Dehradun and Uttarakhand."The most exciting thing for me is that this project has its roots in the beautiful Dehradun Valley and the forests and mountains of Uttarakhand," he said.He added that he was excited about the project bringing recognition to Dehradun and Uttarakhand on a global stage.The announcement was made alongside NSW Treasurer Daniel Mookhey, Australia's first Indian-origin state treasurer, at the reception hosted by the Australian High Commission in New Delhi.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Swiss police report five killed in Dutch tour bus crash
articles.summary: Bus carrying 45 Dutch tourists overturned and landed in a construction zone near an Alpine village.
articles.body:
Five people have been killed and 40 injured in a bus crash in a remote Alpine region of eastern Switzerland, police reported.

Police announced the casualties on Friday, the day after the bus, carrying 45 Dutch tourists, overturned and landed in a construction zone near the village of Susch.

Three of the injured were reported to be in serious condition, with seven moderately hurt and the remaining 30 described as having minor injuries, according to a statement by police in the canton of Grisons.

Seven rescue helicopters and 13 ambulance crews ferried the casualties to hospital. The dead have yet to be identified. Police said they are investigating what caused the crash.

Swiss President Guy Parmelin posted on social media that he was “deeply shocked and dismayed” and offered his “sincere condolences” to the families of the victims.

King Willem-Alexander and Queen Maxima of the Netherlands also sent their condolences.

“Our hearts go out to the bereaved, to everyone currently fearing for the fate of their loved ones and to the injured. We stand with you in this great tragedy,” they wrote on social media.

articles.title: Houthis claim major advance in Yemen and tighten grip on Red Sea shipping lane
articles.summary: The Iran-backed Houthis are also reported to have seized Perim - a strategic island on the major shipping route.
articles.body:
Yemen's Houthis have claimed a major advance on the western Red Sea coast, consolidating their grip on the key international shipping route.

The Iran-backed group seized Perim Island at the mouth of the waterway in the Bab al-Mandab Strait, a source from Yemen's internationally-recognised government told the BBC.

It comes a day after the Houthis captured the strategic port city of Mokha from Saudi-backed pro-government forces, according to military sources. A Yemeni military official told the AFP news agency the Houthis now control the entire coastline.

The Houthis earlier said they posed no threat to international shipping but reiterated their threat to target vessels from Saudi Arabia.

On Friday, Yemeni pro-government forces withdrew from Perim (also known as Mayyun).

Witnesses and news agencies reported that Houthi forces moved on to the island.

The Houthis later issued a statement, saying that their military operation to expel Saudi-backed forces had been a "success" and that "maritime navigation is safe for all companies except for Saudi vessels".

Houthi military spokesman Yahya Sarea said the "large-scale" military operation was launched on 3 September due to Saudi Arabia's "blatant aggression" against "our dear people".

The statement, however, did not mention Perim Island.

Saudi Arabia has not publicly commented on the latest developments.

Perim Island sits at the narrowest point of the Bab al-Mandab Strait, which has become increasingly important following the effective closure of the Strait of Hormuz - another crucial waterway - in the conflict between the US and Iran.

Saudi Arabia has been relying on the Red Sea and the Bab al-Mandab Strait for shipping oil to customers in Asia.

The escalation of the conflict between the Houthis, Yemen's government and Saudi Arabia has contributed to a surge in oil prices.

Hundreds of people have reportedly been killed and thousands displaced since the Houthis launched an offensive in the south-west a week ago.

A Saudi-led coalition has also carried out air strikes on Houthi-controlled areas in western Yemen in support of the pro-government forces, and the Houthis have launched missiles and drones at cities and oil facilities in southern Saudi Arabia.

Since fighting escalated, at least 46,000 people have been displaced in Yemen, according to the International Organization for Migration (IOM).

On Friday, the IOM said the number was "alarmingly rising by the hour".

Amy Pope, IOM director general, said: "Families are being forced to flee for the second or third time in this conflict, with almost nothing left."

The Houthis ousted the internationally recognised government in 2015, triggering Saudi military intervention in the civil war. A truce that had largely held for more than four years effectively collapsed in July.

articles.title: JD(U) renaming on cards? Leaders back proposal to name party after Nitish
articles.summary: India News: NEW DELHI: The Janata Dal (United) is considering a proposal to rename the more than two-decade-old party as ‘JD(U)-Nitish’, in recognition of its sup.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The Janata Dal (United) is considering a proposal to rename the more than two-decade-old party as ‘JD(U)-Nitish’, in recognition of its supreme leader and former Bihar chief minister Nitish Kumar.The suggestion was made by JD(U) working president Sanjay Kumar Jha, who was heard in a purportedly recorded video saying the party owed its standing to Kumar and that its ideology was rooted in his political philosophy.“We should therefore consider renaming the party as JD(U)-Nitish,” Jha was heard saying.The proposal has received backing from senior JD(U) leaders, including Bihar deputy chief minister Bijendra Prasad Yadav and minister Shrawon Kumar.Yadav, a former state president of the JD(U), said, “It is a very good suggestion. Let there be a formal discussion on the matter so that a decision could be taken.”Shrawon Kumar said, “There could not have been a better proposal. I suggest that a formal resolution be brought by the party at the earliest. It is bound to be passed unanimously.”The JD(U) was formed in 2003 through the merger of the Sharad Yadav-led Janata Dal and the Samata Party. Though Sharad Yadav served as its national president until 2016, Nitish Kumar was widely regarded as its de facto leader. Kumar formally took over as national president in 2016.The development comes days after Jha rejected a separate proposal to rename Bakhtiyarpur, Kumar’s birthplace, as ‘Nitishpur’ on Thursday. Responding to the suggestion by Hindustani Awam Morcha national president Santosh Kumar Suman, Jha said Kumar “has always let his work speak on his behalf” and “has never believed in renaming places”.Jha also said, “Let us bear in mind that merely changing the name of the place will not erase from history the fact that Bakhtiyar Khilji had invaded the land and set Nalanda, the ancient seat of learning, on fire”.The proposal to rename the town had also drawn support from Union minister Chirag Paswan. “This is indeed a good suggestion. Nitish Kumar ji has contributed immensely to the progress of Bihar over a long period of time,” Paswan said.The RJD, meanwhile, has criticised both proposals. RJD MLA Bhai Virendra claimed the party could split within months, alleging that the developments pointed in that direction.The JD(U) is yet to announce any formal decision on renaming the party.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: In 2002, San Antonio turned a 1,308-acre Air Force base over to Brooks for redevelopment; 24 years later, after 3,000+ jobs, it is expanding beyond the base with 243 acres
articles.summary: US News: In 2002, San Antonio turned its 1,308-acre decommissioned Air Force base over to the Brooks Development Authority for redevelopment. More than two dec.
articles.body: In 2002, San Antonio turned its 1,308-acre decommissioned Air Force base over to the Brooks Development Authority for redevelopment. More than two decades later, the organisation is looking beyond the former base as it seeks to bring more major employers and development to the city’s Southeast Side.The Brooks Development Authority is taking control of 243 vacant acres south of Loop 410 along Southton Road. The San Antonio River Authority is giving the land to Brooks, which will oversee the work needed to prepare the property, including platting and installing utilities and roads.The move seeks make large areas of land ready for companies looking for locations for major facilities. Officials said the 243-acre property could be attractive because it is close to highways and railway tracks, as well as a proposed east-west freeway known as the South Texas Parkway.Brooks looks beyond the former baseBrooks CEO Leo Gomez said the organisation could use the project as a model for working on other large properties in the area. “If we can do it with this property, we can do it with others,” he said.The Brooks Development Authority was created in 2002 to redevelop the former 1,308-acre Brooks Air Force Base after it was decommissioned. Over the years, the former military property has developed into a mix of residential, commercial and public facilities.The area now has apartments, single-family houses, restaurants, shops, schools, trails, a hospital, a hotel and manufacturing facilities. It has become a significant development area on San Antonio’s South Side, a part of the city that has historically struggled to attract business investment and public amenities.The development authority has attracted companies partly because its land is exempt from property taxes. The area is also designated as a federal opportunity zone and has a tax increment reinvestment zone.More than 1,400 people now live at Brooks, while more than 3,000 people work there. The number is expected to increase as additional housing and facilities are developed. Property values in the area have also increased significantly.However, about 300 acres of the original Brooks footprint remain undeveloped, Gomez said. The development authority has also been considering opportunities outside its original boundaries for several years. Its focus is on sites within about 3 miles of Brooks.Projects outside BrooksIn 2019, Brooks acquired 55 acres near San Antonio State Hospital. Part of that property is being used by SAMMinistries to develop affordable housing and supportive services for people experiencing chronic homelessness.Brooks has also partnered with developer NRP Group on two projects to build tax-exempt, mixed-income apartments.Another major property came under Brooks’ control about three years ago, when the development authority purchased 158 acres of a closed golf course. The land is being leased to Arboretum San Antonio, which plans to turn it into a public space featuring different types of trees and plants.The latest deal gives Brooks another large property to prepare for potential development. Gomez said the idea grew out of conversations with Bexar County Judge Peter Sakai about having sites ready for companies that want to build major facilities.Why the 243 acres matterThe effort is aimed at helping San Antonio compete with other cities when companies are considering locations for large projects.Gomez and other officials referred to the effort as “Project Oso”. “Oso” means “bear” in Spanish. Gomez said he originally believed the Southton property was owned by the county.The land is owned by the San Antonio River Authority, which acquired it in 2007 using county funds. The authority used the property to store dirt removed during construction of the Mission Reach section of the River Walk, which was completed in 2013.The river authority still plans to use the property for storing dirt connected to its work to restore creeks on the West Side. It has permission from Brooks to continue doing so, according to general manager Derek Boese.The property must remain under public ownership. Both the San Antonio River Authority and the Brooks Development Authority are government entities.“This property represents an opportunity to think strategically about the long-term economic future of South San Antonio,” Boese said in a statement.Brooks plans to invest in the siteThe Brooks Development Authority will spend some of its own money to improve the property, Gomez said. It is also likely to seek financial assistance, although he did not specify where that funding would come from. He said the city or county could be possible sources.The development authority sees the Southton property as part of a broader effort rather than an isolated project. The goal is to build on the development that has taken place at the former Air Force base and extend that work into the surrounding area.“Brooks is not stopping at its boundaries. This region is hungry for development,” Gomez said. “Brooks is a tool our community can use to continue what has happened on the former base in the region, and that’s what we intend to do.”Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: From 1947 to 1970, uranium mines supplied America’s defense program; decades later, Montana sealed 20 hazards at five abandoned sites while bat gates preserved wildlife access
articles.summary: US News: Several abandoned uranium mine sites in the Pryor Mountains of south-central Montana have been closed after federal agencies identified safety, radiat.
articles.body: Several abandoned uranium mine sites in the Pryor Mountains of south-central Montana have been closed after federal agencies identified safety, radiation and environmental risks. The work was carried out on lands managed by the Bureau of Land Management (BLM), with the Department of Energy’s Defense Related Uranium Mine (DRUM) programme and other partners involved.The project focused on five historic mine sites where workers addressed dangerous openings and other hazards, according to the information available on BLM's website. In September 2025, contractors completed work to close 20 mine features by backfilling mine openings, installing bat-friendly closure gates, fencing dangerous highwalls, plugging drill holes and removing solid waste.The need for the work was linked to the condition of the abandoned mines. The BLM said entering abandoned mine sites on public lands can be dangerous and, in some cases, fatal. The structures can become unstable over time because they are no longer maintained, increasing the risk of collapse and injury to visitors.Some of the uranium mines in the Pryor Mountains also presented additional risks because of elevated metals and radiation levels in underground workings. The BLM said these levels were linked to remaining mineralisation and were another important reason to prevent public entry into the sites.Work began with detailed site assessmentsThe DRUM programme began assessing abandoned uranium mines in the Pryor Mountains in 2020. Contractors examined the sites for physical hazards, radiation levels and chemical contamination. The assessments helped identify safety risks and determine what reclamation and closure work was required.The sites are part of a much larger national programme. DRUM is a partnership involving the Department of Energy, federal land management agencies, and state and Tribal abandoned mine lands programmes.The mines being addressed under the programme supplied uranium ore to the US Atomic Energy Commission for defence-related activities between 1947 and 1970. The DRUM programme is responsible for helping mitigate safety hazards at these abandoned mine sites.Additional environmental surveys were carried out in 2024. Bat Conservation International (BCI) studied the sites to identify bat habitat, rare plants and cultural resources that could require protection during the closure work.Bats and rare plants were consideredThe presence of wildlife meant that the mine closures had to be planned carefully. BCI personnel worked with an interdisciplinary team of resource specialists to identify biological resources and determine how they should be protected during the project.One of the concerns was bat habitat inside the abandoned mine workings. The project therefore included the installation of bat-friendly closure gates at some mine openings. BCI personnel also relocated a bat before an abandoned mine adit was backfilled.Rare plants were also considered before reclamation work began. BLM Botanist Eric Puetz marked rare plant populations before the mine closure work. One of the plants identified was thick-leaved bladderpod, which the BLM said occurs only in the Pryor Mountain foothills area.The BLM also contacted mining claimants at the sites to ensure that mineral resources remained accessible. After completing the required environmental analysis, the agency issued a decision in August 2025 to proceed with abandoned mine work at multiple sites in the Pryor Mountains.Five sites received closure workThe physical mitigation work was completed in September 2025 by Department of Energy subcontractors from Mountain States Restoration, LLC. Work was carried out at five historic abandoned uranium mine sites.The 20 mine features addressed during the project required different measures depending on the hazards present. Mine openings were backfilled, while bat-compatible gates were installed where appropriate. Dangerous highwalls were fenced, drill holes were plugged and solid waste was removed.The project also involved reclamation measures to help the affected areas recover. A later monitoring visit showed vegetation growing successfully under installed erosion matting at the Swamp Frog mine.However, the BLM said the work does not end when the physical closure is completed. Abandoned mine sites continue to change because of natural processes and human interference.BLM says monitoring will continueDan Seifert, BLM Montana/Dakotas Abandoned Mine Lands and Hazmat programme lead, said continued monitoring is necessary to make sure the closures remain effective."We need to acknowledge that we can't just walk away from these sites after closure work – gravity and erosion continue to occur and mine grates are often vandalized and broken into," Seifert said.The BLM's monitoring work is therefore intended to check whether the closures continue to function and whether additional problems develop at the sites.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: ‘A historic day’: Spain moves closer to citizenship for Western Saharans
articles.summary: Spain’s parliament backs citizenship for Sahrawis amid tense relations with Morocco after the Ceuta crossing.
articles.body:
Madrid, Spain – For Mohamed Mohamedna, it was a historic moment.

On Thursday, the Spanish parliament backed citizenship for Western Saharans born in the North African territory when Madrid ruled it as a colony.

Like other campaigners, 52-year-old Mohamedna had been waiting for years for this gesture.

“This is a great, historic day,” he told Al Jazeera. “I have been living in Spain for 21 years but I have always been classed as having ‘no state’.”

Mohamedna, who has been living in Vitoria in northwestern Spain and works for a private company, has been stateless since he arrived in Spain.

Spain’s lower house of parliament overwhelmingly voted for the move, which analysts say could benefit more than 100,000 Sahrawis.

Mohamedna hopes he will soon be able to apply for a Spanish passport.

But the bill, which requires Senate approval before becoming law, comes amid tensions between Spain and Morocco after more than 70,000 migrants crossed into Spain’s North African enclave of Ceuta in July.

Rabat on Thursday refuted claims by Spanish opposition parties that it had been involved in the mass crossing which caused an international diplomatic row.

The Moroccan foreign ministry said, “Why continue to level accusations against Morocco when no evidence, facts or reports establish any involvement on the part of Moroccan authorities?”

‘Recognise the Sahrawi population’s ties to Spain’

From 1884 until 1976, Western Sahara was under Spanish colonial rule. Morocco has long laid claim to the area, which the United Nations classifies as a non-self-governing territory.

Attempts to organise a referendum on whether it should become independent or a part of Morocco have lagged for years.

Spanish law says it will “recognise the Sahrawi population’s ties to Spain” and would also allow descendants of those granted citizenship to gain it.

According to representatives from the Algeria-backed Polisario Front, the independence movement which has fought for freedom for the territory from Morocco, some 110,000 Sahrawis could be eligible for Spanish citizenship.

Once the law takes effect, applicants have three years in order – extendable to four years – to seek citizenship. Up to 70,000 Sahrawis can get Spanish citizenship as well as their direct descendants – their sons or daughters – who will have five years to apply after their parents are registered.

Sahrawis will be eligible to access nationality by residence via an accelerated route, needing only two years of legal residence in Spain instead of 10 years generally required for nationality.

This will put them on equal standing with citizens of most Latin American countries, Sephardic Jews, nationals of the Philippines, Equatorial Guinea and Portugal.

The bill was passed by 168 votes in favour with 31 votes against.

The ruling Socialists, the far-left Sumar and other regional parties supported the bill, while the opposition conservative People’s Party (PP) abstained and the far-right Vox party voted against it.

“With the adoption of this legislation, we are restoring – and I emphasise, restoring – the Spanish national identity card to those Sahrawis who once held it and from whom this state took it away,” said Tesh Sidi of the leftist Sumar coalition, who is the first woman of Sahrawi origin to serve in parliament, Reuters reported.

Spain and Morocco have a sticky diplomatic relationship over issues including migration, airspace, territorial waters, customs and land borders.

Pablo Simon, a political analyst at the University Carlos III in Madrid, warned of a clash with Morocco.

“There are always reasons for confrontations between Spain and Morocco,” he told Al Jazeera. “But this is a historic [restoration of nationality] on the part of Spain. Even the opposition PP has abstained.”

However, Rabat has not officially condemned the citizenship move for Sahrawis.

In 2020, Morocco agreed to reopen its diplomatic mission in Tel Aviv as part of the Abraham Accords signed during United States President Donald Trump’s first term. In return, the US recognised Moroccan sovereignty over Western Sahara.

Last year, the US government said it was authorising major investments in Moroccan-controlled Western Sahara.

The Polisario Front independence movement seeks recognition of an independent state called the Sahrawi Arab Democratic Republic. Many Sahrawis live in refugee camps in Tindouf, Algeria, or elsewhere abroad, while others remain in Western Sahara.

Spain had supported a referendum in the territory – in line with UN resolutions – until Pedro Sanchez’s government made a surprise change of policy in 2022 and backed Morocco’s position.

The policy switch came in the wake of the crossing of more than 8,000 migrants into Ceuta in 2021. Rabat said it had allowed the migrants to cross the border from Morocco into the Spanish enclave in reprisal for Spain treating a Polisario leader, Brahim Ghali, in hospital in Logrono for COVID.

Tensions eased somewhat after the shift, with Madrid describing Rabat’s autonomy proposal for Western Sahara as “serious, credible and realistic”.

The law which has granted citizenship to Sahrawis is part of a series of initiatives under the so-called “grandchildren law”, which allowed descendants of Spaniards who went into exile or emigrated during the Spanish Civil War, between 1936-1939 and during the dictatorship of General Francisco Franco until 1975, to claim citizenship.

In a move to avoid controversy with Morocco, the Socialist government agreed to remove the words “Sahrawi people” and replace it with “Sahrawi population” or simply “Sahrawis”. But this upset the Socialists’ left-wing allies, Sumar, and they were defeated.

To prove Sahrawi status, applicants may show a variety of documents, including a receipt showing registration on the United Nations roll for the Western Sahara self-determination referendum, which never took place as it was banned by Rabat.

Other examples of proof include a driver’s licence, a pension payment receipt, and other documents issued by a Spanish administration showing birth in the territory before September 29, 1977.

“We have been fighting for this for many years and finally it has come to pass,” said Mohamedna.

articles.title: I moved my shop 20 miles because I couldn't afford £300 a week on fuel
articles.summary: People in Turriff, Aberdeenshire, tell BBC Scotland News the impact rising petrol prices is having.
articles.body:
Antique shop owner Melanie Wilson says she has moved her business closer to home because she was struggling to pay nearly £300 a week on diesel as a result of soaring fuel prices.

She opened her new location in Turriff, Aberdeenshire, earlier this month - cutting her commute by 20 miles and her fuel spend in half.

Fuel prices in the UK have climbed about 5p in just one week as a result of the ongoing conflict in the Middle East, with diesel edging towards £1.95 a litre in some areas.

Wilson is one of countless people in small rural locations around Scotland who are feeling the pinch as they need their cars for work and everyday life.

Why are petrol and diesel prices rising again?

Fuel prices started to climb when the US-Israel war with Iran began on 28 February.

The military strikes severely disrupted the production and transportation of energy across the region.

Prices fell back when the US and Iran agreed to a framework deal to end the fighting in June.

However they have started rising again as tensions resurface, with the price of wholesale oil back above $100 a barrel.

More stories from North East Scotland, Orkney and Shetland

Listen to news from North East Scotland on BBC Sounds

Wilson, 37, lives in Banff, but has now moved her shop location from Insch to Turriff to cut travel costs.

She said she spends more than £150 a week on diesel - but it used to be about double that.

"I decided to move the shop really just because of the travel," she said.

"It just wasn't justifiable driving back and forth every day with the price of fuel. It's scary.

"There's no other option. I mean, you can dread going to the pump."

Taxi driver Martin Milne, 55, employs 24 people at his business.

With fuel obviously forming a significant part of the company's running costs, rising prices are putting further pressure on his business.

"The last two days the price has risen nine, 10 pence a litre," he said.

"The cost per month now to fill my cars is horrendous. It's getting more and more every time, you can't see a way out of this now, it makes it very difficult.

"I would say a monthly fuel would be £6,500, before the Iran conflict it was maybe £5,000."

For her, having a car means being able to get out and about independently.

However, she too is feeling the impact of higher fuel costs.

"Well it's rather expensive, it certainly makes you wonder if you'll put your heating on or not," she said.

"I am definitely having to make those choices. It'll never come back down - it's gone up, and it won't come back down I can guarantee that.

"I just don't go so far with the car now, I just think I can cut back that way.

"I can still go out and walk and get the heat up that way."

Driver John Reid, 37, spends a lot of time on the road.

"To keep the truck on the road, it's quite expensive," he said.

"It's just the way it is right now, the price is up and down here all the time.

"The prices are getting extortionate, that's the truth about it."

Carer Jared Whitehouse, 42, does a lot of miles in his car, and his bike.

He said his costs have gone up drastically.

"Yesterday I came out of Aberdeen and I paid £80 to fill the tank - compared to probably a couple of few years ago where I was paying like closer to £60.

"I've been doing a lot more riding around on my bike, because it's just cheaper."

Tyreece Flaws, 25, who works in road haulage, lives in Portsoy and works in Turriff.

"I travel quite far for work, about 25 miles each way, so it's quite expensive.

"When I pull up at the forecourt I just kind of close my eyes and hope for the best.

"I have zero option, I have to drive for work, so I have to fill up. Doesn't help with the rest of the cost of living, food and stuff. I do worry about money."

How do wholesale oil prices affect the cost of petrol and diesel at the pump?

Crude oil is a key ingredient in petrol and diesel, which means that higher wholesale costs make filling up a car more expensive. The price of petrol and diesel is also heavily influenced by demand and refining capacity.

Analysts say every $10 (£7.44) per barrel increase in the oil price pushes up pump prices by roughly 7p a litre.

Since the war began, the price of a barrel of Brent crude - the global benchmark for wholesale oil prices - has been very volatile.

Generally speaking, news of further conflict drives the price up while hopes of an end to the war pushes the price down.

Before the conflict, Brent was about $70 a barrel, but the fighting saw it peak at above $120.

In early July, after the framework deal was signed, prices fell back to near the $70 a barrel mark.

When the peace talks collapsed, the price climbed back up again to above $100 a barrel. It fell back for a few weeks but is once again over the $100 mark after a fresh escalation in hostilities.

articles.title: Myanmar airport closed following reported drone attack
articles.summary: Military government pins attack on pro-democracy rebels it has been battling since seizing power in 2021.
articles.body:
Flight operations ‌at Myanmar’s second-busiest airport have been halted, as the country’s military-backed government accused rebel groups of attempted drone attacks.

Myanmar Airways International said on its Facebook page late on Thursday that all international flights from Mandalay’s Tada-U International Airport on September 11 and 12 had been cancelled.

Domestic flights were being transferred to a nearby airport until further notice for “operational reasons”, the statement added.

The state-run Global New Light of Myanmar outlet reported that security forces had thwarted an attack on the airport by the People’s Defence Force. It said the pro-democracy rebel group had fired six “suicide drones” at ⁠the facility.

“The attack temporarily disrupted some ⁠domestic flights. However, no casualties or damage to vehicles or airport runways were reported,” the newspaper said.

Local media reported that resistance forces were targeting military jet fighters ⁠at the airport, although the situation could not be independently verified by Al Jazeera or news agencies.

Myanmar has been gripped by ⁠conflict since the ousting of an elected ⁠government led by Aung San Suu Kyi in a February 2021 coup, prompting a nationwide resistance movement that has evolved into a civil war between the ‌military and an array of armed ethnic and pro-democracy groups.

Min Aung Hlaing, Myanmar’s former military government chief, was elected president ‌by ‌a military-backed parliament in April, formalising his grip on power after five years of army rule.

This human rights situation in Myanmar has plummeted “to a new low,” according to the United Nations , citing “brutal abuse” of the Rohingya minority and the devastating impact of illicit economic activity, including illegal mining for rare earths.

Rebel groups and Myanmar’s military are now both using drones in the protracted civil war, which has killed more than 100,000 people, according to the Armed Conflict Location and Event Data (ACLED) project.

articles.title: Beverley Knight to sing Dolly Parton at Last Night of the Proms
articles.summary: The Wolverhampton singer will perform I Will Always Love You as part of a tribute to the late star.
articles.body:
Wolverhampton singer Beverley Knight is to perform one of Dolly Parton's best-known songs at this year's Last Night of the Proms.

Knight will sing I Will Always Love You as part of To Dolly, With Love, a tribute to the late country music star at the Royal Albert Hall on Saturday.

The medley, arranged by Fiona Bryce, also features Sheridan Smith performing 9 to 5 and country-pop duo Ward Thomas singing Jolene.

Parton died in August having had a seven-decade career gaining 10 Grammy awards and selling more than 100 million records worldwide. She was also known for her humanitarian work.

Knight's career has spanned more than 30 years, with the Wolverhampton-born singer known for hits including Shoulda Woulda Coulda and Get Up .

She has also played starring roles in the musicals The Bodyguard , Cats and The Drifters Girl .

The 2026 Proms season has included 86 concerts, with 72 Proms at the Royal Albert Hall and 14 at venues around the UK.

The Last Night programme will also feature world premieres by British composer Anne Dudley and Canadian composer and conductor Samy Moussa.

International pianist Yuja Wang will make her Proms debut performing Samuel Barber's Piano Concerto , while Scottish tenor Nicky Spence will perform excerpts from Antonín Dvořák's Rusalka and Frank Loesser's Guys and Dolls .

The traditional finale will include Rule, Britannia! , Jerusalem , Elgar's Pomp and Circumstance March No. 1 and Auld Lang Syne .

The Last Night of the Proms will be broadcast live on BBC Radio 3 from 19:10 BST Saturday bringing the BBC Proms' eight-week 2026 season to a close. It can also be seen on BBC 2 and BBC 1 and iPlayer.

articles.title: Virginia teacher and her husband feared their farms could become subdivisions or data centres; then he died, but she protected 215 acres with limits that bind future owners
articles.summary: US News: Becky Shelton could have cashed in, just like many other landowners in her neighbourhood. But she knew that wasn’t what she and her late husband wante.
articles.body: Becky Shelton could have cashed in, just like many other landowners in her neighbourhood. But she knew that wasn’t what she and her late husband wanted. Selling the 215 acres to developers reshaping Northern Virginia was everything against their dream. So, she went as planned and locked the land away, ensuring that it never becomes housing subdivisions or data centres.A conservation easement on her King George property, and a purchase of development rights on the Stafford acreage where she lives, helped her get there. These two legal protections mean the land will remain woods, pastures and crops. The restrictions bind not just her, but every owner who comes after.Steward of the landBecky Shelton came to the area decades ago to attend what was then Mary Washington College. She never left. She taught everything from general subjects to special education, watching generations of students pass through her classroom. Besides working as a teacher, she also raised animals and crops on her land, watching the seasons turn over on those 215 acres.Soon, she grew a connection with the land. She believes in the philosophy that one never owns the land; they only take care of it. “I have always felt, as Native Americans would say, that we never really own property. Instead, we need to be stewards of the land today and take care of it until the next person can take care of it tomorrow. And to me, taking care of it means keeping it and leaving it as natural as possible and still beautiful,” Shelton said, according to a newsletter by Northern Neck Land Conservancy.That very philosophy shapes how she talks about her properties. She feels she is only borrowing them for today, kind of a temporary stewardship situation. “I’ve never spoken about this as ‘my land’. For a lifetime I’m going to do the best I can with it, then turn it over to somebody else who loves it.”The easements make this intention legal and permanent. Once restricted, the land stays restricted regardless of who owns it next. Future buyers inherit the covenant along with the deed. This makes any development impossible. The rules stay forever: pastures cannot become subdivisions; the fields cannot become data centres.She and her recently deceased husband had agreed that they didn’t want their lands covered in subdivision homes or data centres. They wanted them to stay the way they were. So, she ensured it happened.Protecting Muddy CreekBecky and her husband were worried about their land being engulfed in Northern Virginia’s recent land boom. He’s gone now, but she didn’t wait for developers to circle. She ensured the land remains protected from development. So, she placed a conservation easement, held by Northern Neck Land Conservancy, on her 128-acre farm property in King George County. There’s more. Becky also protected the 87-acre farm where she lives along Bethel Church Road through Stafford County’s purchase of development rights programme. These programmes will protect the land from development, including subdivision homes and data centres.She is truly happy that her land stays the way it is supposed to be. One afternoon, as Shelton walked the 128 acres bordering Muddy Creek, the waterway dividing Stafford and King George counties, she pointed out an oyster fossil at the creek’s edge where water trickled over stony ledges. An eagle cut lazy circles through the pines overhead. “Earlier this year, there was a waterfall here when there was so much more water coming through. It’s interesting how things change with the seasons,” Shelton said.The seasonal shifts are what pulled her to this place and what she fights to preserve. Some people dream of holidays. Shelton wanted only to stay on the farm, tending hay and corn, watching the landscape move through its cycles. “Some people talk about the vacations they’ve been on or want to take, but I always just wanted to be here on the farm. There’s something unique and soothing about nature, which is why I want this to stay as it is,” she said.She could have sold it, especially as property values in Northern Virginia have soared. The money would have been substantial. But nothing could have matched the same peace her land brings. She not only protected the land like a steward, but also ensured it would never be anyone’s to develop.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Meet Cliff Linster, the Wyoming fossil collector whose bizarre Jurassic “squid” sat for 30 years before being recognised as a new species to science
articles.summary: US News: For nearly 30 years, an unusually chunky Jurassic fossil lay waiting to reveal what it was. Fossil collector Cliff Linster discovered one of only two .
articles.body: For nearly 30 years, an unusually chunky Jurassic fossil lay waiting to reveal what it was. Fossil collector Cliff Linster discovered one of only two known specimens in Wyoming, and his find was donated to the Wyoming Dinosaur Centre in 2019. Scientists have now identified it as Wyoteuthis linsterorum, a previously unknown species of belemnite dating to around 160 million years. Unlike the familiar bullet-shaped fossils commonly found in Wyoming, this ancient squid relative had a remarkably broad, barrel-shaped rostrum, earning it the description of the “chunkiest” belemnite ever found. The discovery also revealed a rare surviving branch of an ancient lineage.What did Cliff Linster’s Wyoming fossil reveal about a Jurassic “squid”According to the study published in Wiley, titled ‘‘The big chunky belemnite: a new relict megateuthidid from the Oxfordian (Late Jurassic) of Wyoming, USA, and its place in the evolutionary history of the group, " the specimen was found in situ in Bighorn County, about six miles south of Hyattville, in a sandstone layer containing smaller belemnites and Camptonectes shells. It came from the upper part of the Redwater Shale, within Wyoming’s Sundance Formation, a geological unit formed when an inland sea covered part of the western United States.What made the fossil stand out was its extraordinary shape. Typical Wyoming belemnites have bullet-shaped remains measuring roughly 5 to 10 centimetres long and just 1 to 2 centimetres wide. By contrast, Wyoteuthis linsterorum had a broad, barrel-shaped rostrum around 10 centimetres long and as much as six centimetres wide. Researchers estimate that the animal itself may have reached about 60 centimetres in length, including its arms.Why was Cliff Linster’s Jurassic “squid” fossil so unusualBelemnites were ancient cephalopods related to modern squid and octopuses, and their hard, bullet-shaped rostra are among the most recognisable marine fossils of the Mesozoic. In Wyoming, they are so common that palaeontologist Jessica Lippincott says they are informally “squid butts”. Linster’s specimen, however, was anything but ordinary.The fossil belonged to the Megateuthididae, a belemnite that flourished mainly during the Early to Middle Jurassic and was generally thought to have disappeared much earlier. The researchers concluded that Wyoteuthis was a rare surviving branch of that lineage in the Late Jurassic, making its presence in Wyoming especially significant.Two Wyoming fossils help scientists identify a new speciesAccording to the University of Manchester, the first known specimen was found in the late 1990s by Burkhard Pohl, founder of the Wyoming Dinosaur Centre; he noticed a belemnite was much larger than the ones he normally encountered. That specimen then remained unstudied in the museum collection for years.After Linster found the second specimen and donated it in 2019, researchers had the two examples needed to recognise and formally describe the animal. CT scanning allowed scientists to examine internal structures without damaging the fossils, helping establish their unusual anatomical characteristics and their relationship to the long-lost Megateuthididae lineage.Why was the new Jurassic “squid” named after Cliff LinsterThe new animal’s scientific name honours Linster and his family. The genus name Wyoteuthis combines Wyoming’s abbreviation with the Greek word for squid, meaning essentially “a squid from Wyoming”, while linsterorum recognises the Linster family. The researchers specifically acknowledged Linster for discovering the holotype and donating it, making the specimen available for scientific study.Lippincott said the fossil was unlike anything she had encountered during years of collecting Wyoming’s common Pachyteuthis belemnites, adding that the discovery showed how rockhounds and invertebrate fossil collectors can contribute to science. Linster died in June 2026, but he knew researchers were studying his find and was excited that it would be formally described. British palaeontologist Dean Lomax, who had previously collected fossils with Linster and his wife Sandy, said it was “bittersweet” that Linster did not live to see the publication, but that naming the fossil after him would preserve his family name in palaeontology.Catch the latest World News and Live updates.
